description: Per-recipient daily cap vectors: the UTC day window, early rejection at request, the binding check at execute and the midnight edge.

vectors.description: Two recipients each receive exactly the daily cap of 500 on one day; their usage is kept apart, keyed by recipient_ref.
With 400 of a daily cap of 500 executed, a request for 101 is DAILY_CAP_EXCEEDED and one for exactly 100 is allowed.
Requests do not use the daily cap, so two of 500 are both allowed; executing them together or one after the other fails the second.
Two payouts to one recipient in one execute batch accumulate, 300 then 200, to exactly the daily cap of 500.
A full cap paid at 23:59:59 counts on day 20454 and blocks 1 more that second; at 00:00:00 day 20455 starts with the whole cap.
A payout requested on day 20454, when that day's cap is then used up, executes at 00:00:00 and counts on day 20455.
A payout requested on day 20454 and executed on day 20455 is DAILY_CAP_EXCEEDED once that day's cap is used.
With 400 executed, lowering the daily cap to 300 leaves no headroom, not a negative one: 1 is refused at request and at execute.
Two destinations bound to #bob share one daily cap: after 300 to bob, 201 to bob_bank is refused and 200 fills the cap.
daily_used names today with nothing used once the stored day has passed, and for a recipient never paid.
The day a recipient reaches the cap a request is refused; the next day daily_used shows nothing used and the same request passes.
